content.value: Declare and overload constructors; initialize object state from parameters; distinguish constructors from similarly named methods.

A constructor uses exactly the class name and has no return type. It executes when new creates an instance and establishes the object’s initial state. Parameters allow callers to supply initialization values. They are not automatically persistent fields; explicitly copy or transform them into the object’s representation.

Constructors may be overloaded with different parameter lists. If a class declares no constructor, Java supplies a no-argument constructor. Once you declare a constructor yourself, an additional no-argument form is not supplied automatically. Document and respect initialization preconditions so later methods begin with valid state.

new Ticket() stores 10. new Ticket(25) stores 25 in a different object. The overload is selected from the argument list. Neither constructor returns a price; getPrice is a separate method that observes the initialized field.

public void Ticket() is a method, not a constructor. A class with only Ticket(int) cannot be constructed with new Ticket() unless you also declare that form. Do not accidentally initialize a local variable while leaving the field at its default.

Add a constructor parameter for quantity and store price * quantity as total, assuming both are nonnegative. Test zero quantity and one quantity, and state how you would handle invalid negative inputs.
